newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees Q4 charges from cost cutting.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees Q4 charges from cost cutting.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Tuesday it expects it will take charges of "tens of millions of dollars" in the fourth quarter as part of its effort to cut costs in its semiconductor and other groups.
The technology giant said it has cut costs by reducing its work force and halting building projects. Motorola said additional actions will be taken in the fourth quarter.

"Those charges will be in the several tens of millions of dollars. They will apply not only to our semiconductor sector but also to some of our other businesses," Ed Gams, director of investor relations, told analysts in a conference call.

"We need to finalize these actions, make the notifications that are required of those affected and then public statements would be made," Gams said, declining to give further details about the measures underway.
On Monday Motorola reported significantly lower third quarter earnings of $0.34 a share versus $0.81 last year. According to First Call, analysts' consensus third quarter estimate was $0.35 a share.
The company cited among other things the generally soft semiconductor industry and stiff competition in pricing of cellular telephones.

Gams said the company believes the semiconductor industry's recent recession may have bottomed out, but it still expects year-over-year industry order growth and revenues to remain negative for a few more quarters.

Motorola projected an industry-wide revenue decline of 10 percent for 1996 but growth for 1997, citing "a rate of less than 10 percent". Last year the worldwide semiconductor industry had revenues of $145.9 billion, the company said.
Gams said, however, the company sees continued under-utilized capacity in the industry, prohibiting the possibility of a significant rise in semiconductor prices.

"This will continue to place significant pressure on our semiconductor profitability," Gams said. "(A) return to double-digit operating margins for the full year of 1997 for our semiconductor sector does not appear to be achievable."
Motorola said its semiconductor group essentially broke even in the third quarter.
The Schaumburg, Ill.-based company reiterated that stiff pricing competition has also affected its cellular telephone, paging and modem businesses.
"Pricing remains very competitive in all our major businesses and we expect this to continue," Gams said.

Overall orders were up five percent, Gams said, but excluding a catch-up in order recognition for the Iridium global telecommunications project, orders fell five percent. Motorola has a 25 percent stake in the Iridium LLC consortium.

According to Gams, Iridium LLC's losses are expected to rise next year as a result of depreciation and operations and staffing expenses associated with the deployment of satellites, due to begin in late 1996 or early 1997.
"Iridium LLC losses are expected to increase by several hundred million dollars in 1997 versus 1996," Gams said.
